lesson_scope: Special completing the square forms including negative leading coefficients A - (x-b)^2, factored bracket forms (kx+a)^2 + b, factored-out whole bracket forms a[(x+c)^2 + d], maximum/minimum deduction, line of symmetry, range, and parametric geometric distances.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: basic negative-leading monic completing the square into maximum form A - (x - b)^2.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of factoring -1 before completing the square to obtain A - (x - b)^2.

hints: Rearrange the terms: $-x^2 + 4x + 7$.
Factor $-1$ from the $x$-terms: $-(x^2 - 4x) + 7$, remembering to reverse the sign of $4x$.
Complete the square: $x^2 - 4x = (x - 2)^2 - 4$, then distribute the minus sign: $-(x - 2)^2 + 4 + 7 = 11 - (x - 2)^2$.

walkthrough.text:
Rearrange the expression in standard order and factor out $-1$ from the terms in $x$:
$$7 + 4x - x^2 = -(x^2 - 4x) + 7$$

Complete the square for $x^2 - 4x$ inside the bracket:
$$x^2 - 4x = (x - 2)^2 - 4$$
$$-(x^2 - 4x) + 7 = -\left((x - 2)^2 - 4\right) + 7$$

Distribute the minus sign and combine the constant terms:
$$= -(x - 2)^2 + 4 + 7 = 11 - (x - 2)^2$$
Thus $A = 11, b = 2$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: reading maximum point coordinates and maximum value from A - (x - b)^2 form.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of reading vertex and maximum value from negative vertex form.

hints: The subtracted square $-(x + 3)^2 \le 0$ attains its maximum of $0$ when $x + 3 = 0$.
Set $x + 3 = 0 \implies x = -3$, giving the maximum value $y = 15 - 0 = 15$.

walkthrough.text:
The maximum point occurs where the subtracted squared term is zero:
$$x + 3 = 0 \implies x = -3$$

State the maximum value:
$$\text{Maximum value} = 15$$

ai_rubric.observable: States the maximum point coordinates as $(-3, 15)$.
States that the maximum value of $y$ is $15$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: factoring the whole expression into a[(x+c)^2 + d] form.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of keeping a common factor outside the entire completed square bracket.

hints: Factor $2$ out of all three terms: $2(x^2 + 4x + 7)$.
Complete the square for $x^2 + 4x + 7$ inside the bracket: $(x + 2)^2 - 4 + 7 = (x + 2)^2 + 3$.
Keep the outer factor $2$ surrounding the entire bracket: $2[(x + 2)^2 + 3]$.

walkthrough.text:
Factor out $2$ from every term of the quadratic:
$$2x^2 + 8x + 14 = 2(x^2 + 4x + 7)$$

Complete the square for $x^2 + 4x + 7$:
$$x^2 + 4x + 7 = (x + 2)^2 - 4 + 7 = (x + 2)^2 + 3$$

Write the expression in the required form $2[(x + c)^2 + d]$:
$$2x^2 + 8x + 14 = 2\left[(x + 2)^2 + 3\right]$$
Thus $c = 2, d = 3$.

ai_rubric.observable: Factors $2$ from the whole quadratic $2(x^2 + 4x + 7)$ and forms $2[(x + 2)^2 - 4 + 7]$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: non-monic negative leading coefficient completing the square into q - a(x - p)^2 form.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of non-monic negative quadratic completing the square.

hints: Factor $-2$ out of the first two terms: $-2(x^2 - 6x) + 5$.
Complete the square: $x^2 - 6x = (x - 3)^2 - 9$.

walkthrough.text:
Factor $-2$ from the $x$-terms:
$$5 + 12x - 2x^2 = -2(x^2 - 6x) + 5$$

Complete the square for $x^2 - 6x$ inside the bracket:
$$x^2 - 6x = (x - 3)^2 - 9$$
$$-2(x^2 - 6x) + 5 = -2\left((x - 3)^2 - 9\right) + 5$$

Distribute $-2$ and combine constants:
$$= -2(x - 3)^2 + 18 + 5 = 23 - 2(x - 3)^2$$
Thus $q = 23, p = 3$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: completing the square directly into the (2x + a)^2 + b form for a quadratic with perfect square leading coefficient.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of expanding (2x + a)^2 + b to match coefficients.

hints: Expand $(2x + a)^2 + b = 4x^2 + 4ax + a^2 + b$.
Equate linear coefficients: $4a = 12 \implies a = 3$.
Compute $a^2 = 9$, then find $b = 13 - 9 = 4$ to obtain $(2x + 3)^2 + 4$.

walkthrough.text:
Expand the required form $(2x + a)^2 + b$:
$$(2x + a)^2 + b = 4x^2 + 4ax + a^2 + b$$

Equate the linear term with $4x^2 + 12x + 13$:
$$4a = 12 \implies a = 3$$

Equate the constant term:
$$a^2 + b = 13 \implies 3^2 + b = 13 \implies 9 + b = 13 \implies b = 4$$
$$(2x + 3)^2 + 4$$

ai_rubric.observable: Expands $(2x + a)^2 + b = 4x^2 + 4ax + a^2 + b$ and identifies $4a = 12 \implies a = 3$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: deducing the range of a negative quadratic function from vertex form.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of determining range for a negative parabola.

hints: For all real $x$, $-3(x - 4)^2 \le 0$ because any squared real number is non-negative.
The maximum value of $f(x)$ is $10$, achieved at $x = 4$, so the range is $f(x) \le 10$.

walkthrough.text:
For all real $x \in \mathbb{R}$, $(x - 4)^2 \ge 0$, which means:
$$-3(x - 4)^2 \le 0$$

State the range of the function:
$$\text{Range: } f(x) \le 10 \quad (\text{or } y \le 10)$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Easy: negative-leading quadratic completing the square into the standard Cambridge maximum form A - (x - b)^2 with integer arithmetic.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: The source requires completing the square for a negative quadratic into A - (x - b)^2.

hints: Rearrange into standard descending order: $-x^2 + 6x + 10$.
Factor $-1$ from the $x$-terms: $-(x^2 - 6x) + 10$, noting the sign change inside the bracket.
Complete the square for $x^2 - 6x = (x - 3)^2 - 9$, then distribute the minus sign: $-(x - 3)^2 + 9 + 10 = 19 - (x - 3)^2$.

walkthrough.text:
Write the quadratic in standard descending order:
$$10 + 6x - x^2 = -x^2 + 6x + 10$$

Factor out $-1$ from the terms in $x$:
$$-(x^2 - 6x) + 10$$

Complete the square inside the bracket for $x^2 - 6x$:
$$x^2 - 6x = (x - 3)^2 - 9$$
$$-(x^2 - 6x) + 10 = -\left((x - 3)^2 - 9\right) + 10 = -(x - 3)^2 + 9 + 10 = 19 - (x - 3)^2$$

State the integer constants:
$$A = 19, \quad b = 3$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Easy: factored-out whole bracket form a[(x+c)^2 + d] and deduction of the minimum value.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: The source requires the factored-out bracket form 2[(x+1)^2 + 5]; this original question uses factor 3.

hints: Factor out $3$ from every term of the quadratic: $3(x^2 + 6x + 13)$.
Complete the square on the monic quadratic inside the brackets: $x^2 + 6x + 13 = (x + 3)^2 - 9 + 13 = (x + 3)^2 + 4$.
Keep the outer factor $3$ outside the brackets to write $3[(x + 3)^2 + 4]$, and evaluate the minimum value $3 \times 4 = 12$ when $(x + 3)^2 = 0$.

walkthrough.text:
Factor $3$ from the entire expression:
$$3x^2 + 18x + 39 = 3(x^2 + 6x + 13)$$

Complete the square for $x^2 + 6x + 13$ inside the square brackets:
$$x^2 + 6x + 13 = (x + 3)^2 - 3^2 + 13 = (x + 3)^2 - 9 + 13 = (x + 3)^2 + 4$$

Combine with the external factor $3$:
$$3x^2 + 18x + 39 = 3\left[(x + 3)^2 + 4\right]$$
So $c = 3$ and $d = 4$.

Determine the minimum value:
$$\text{Since } (x + 3)^2 \ge 0, \quad \text{Minimum value} = 3(0 + 4) = 12$$

ai_rubric.observable: Factors $3$ from the whole quadratic $3(x^2 + 6x + 13)$ and completes the square inside.
States that the minimum value is $12$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: completing the square into (3x + a)^2 + b by expansion and coefficient matching for a quadratic with 9x^2 leading term.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Assesses non-standard bracket form (3x + a)^2 + b with 9x^2.

hints: Expand the target form $(3x + a)^2 + b = 9x^2 + 6ax + a^2 + b$.
Equate the linear coefficients: $6a = -24$ to find $a = -4$.
Compute $a^2 = (-4)^2 = 16$, then equate the constant terms: $16 + b = 23$.
Solve for $b = 23 - 16 = 7$, giving $(3x - 4)^2 + 7$.

walkthrough.text:
Expand the target expression $(3x + a)^2 + b$:
$$(3x + a)^2 + b = 9x^2 + 6ax + a^2 + b$$

Equate the coefficient of $x$ to find $a$:
$$6a = -24 \implies a = -4$$

Equate the constant terms to find $b$:
$$a^2 + b = 23 \implies (-4)^2 + b = 23 \implies 16 + b = 23 \implies b = 7$$

Write down the final expression:
$$(3x - 4)^2 + 7$$

ai_rubric.observable: Expands $(3x + a)^2 + b = 9x^2 + 6ax + a^2 + b$ and equates $6a = -24$ to find $a = -4$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: negative non-monic completing the square with leading coefficient -2, leading to maximum point coordinates and range.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Requires completing the square for 7 + 8x - 2x^2 into q - 2(x + p)^2 form.

hints: Factor $-2$ from the $x$-terms: $-2(x^2 - 4x) + 7$.
Complete the square: $x^2 - 4x = (x - 2)^2 - 4$.

walkthrough.text:
Factor out $-2$ from the quadratic and linear terms:
$$7 + 8x - 2x^2 = -2(x^2 - 4x) + 7$$

Complete the square for $x^2 - 4x$ inside the bracket:
$$x^2 - 4x = (x - 2)^2 - 4$$
$$-2(x^2 - 4x) + 7 = -2\left((x - 2)^2 - 4\right) + 7$$

Distribute $-2$ and simplify constants:
$$= -2(x - 2)^2 + 8 + 7 = 15 - 2(x - 2)^2$$
Thus $q = 15$ and $p = -2$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Extracts maximum coordinates and range from completed-square form.

hints: The maximum point occurs where the squared bracket is zero: $x - 2 = 0 \implies x = 2$.
At $x = 2$, $y = 15 - 0 = 15$, giving maximum coordinates $(2, 15)$.
Since $-2(x - 2)^2 \le 0$, all function outputs satisfy $f(x) \le 15$.

walkthrough.text:
The maximum point occurs where the subtracted squared term is zero:
$$x - 2 = 0 \implies x = 2$$
$$y = 15 - 2(0)^2 = 15$$
$$\text{Maximum point} = (2, 15)$$

Because $-2(x - 2)^2 \le 0$ for all real $x$, the function takes all values less than or equal to $15$:
$$\text{Range: } f(x) \le 15 \quad (\text{or } y \le 15)$$

ai_rubric.observable: States the coordinates of the maximum point as $(2, 15)$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: completing the square into (2x + p)^2 + q form for 4x^2 + 20x + 31, finding the minimizing x-value and the line of symmetry.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Tests completed square form (2x + p)^2 + q with 4x^2 leading term.

hints: Expand $(2x + p)^2 + q = 4x^2 + 4px + p^2 + q$.
Match the linear term: $4p = 20 \implies p = 5$.
Evaluate $p^2 = 25$, then find $q = 31 - 25 = 6$ to write $(2x + 5)^2 + 6$.

walkthrough.text:
Expand the target form $(2x + p)^2 + q$:
$$(2x + p)^2 + q = 4x^2 + 4px + p^2 + q$$

Equate the coefficient of $x$ to determine $p$:
$$4p = 20 \implies p = 5$$

Equate the constant terms to determine $q$:
$$p^2 + q = 31 \implies 5^2 + q = 31 \implies 25 + q = 31 \implies q = 6$$
$$(2x + 5)^2 + 6$$

ai_rubric.observable: Expands $(2x + p)^2 + q = 4x^2 + 4px + p^2 + q$ and equates $4p = 20$ to find $p = 5$.
Sets $5^2 + q = 31$ to find $q = 6$ and obtains $(2x + 5)^2 + 6$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Deduces the minimizing x-value and the line of symmetry from (2x+p)^2 + q.

hints: The minimum occurs where the bracket is zero: $2x + 5 = 0$.
Solve $2x + 5 = 0$ to get $x = -\dfrac{5}{2}$ (or $x = -2.5$).
The vertical line of symmetry is $x = -\dfrac{5}{2}$.

walkthrough.text:
The minimum value occurs when the squared bracket vanishes:
$$2x + 5 = 0 \implies 2x = -5 \implies x = -\frac{5}{2} \quad (\text{or } x = -2.5)$$

The line of symmetry is the vertical line through the minimum point:
$$x = -\frac{5}{2} \quad (\text{or } x = -2.5)$$

ai_rubric.observable: States $x = -\dfrac{5}{2}$ (or $x = -2.5$) for the minimum value location.
States the equation of the line of symmetry as $x = -\dfrac{5}{2}$ (or $x = -2.5$).

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: parametric negative completing the square into M(k) - (x - k)^2 form and solving a linear condition on maximum value to locate the vertex.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Applies parametric negative completing the square.

hints: Factor $-1$ from the $x$-terms: $-(x^2 - 2kx) - (k^2 - 4k + 12)$.
Complete the square for $x^2 - 2kx$: $(x - k)^2 - k^2$.
Distribute the minus sign: $-\left((x - k)^2 - k^2\right) = -(x - k)^2 + k^2$.
Combine with $-(k^2 - 4k + 12)$ to obtain $M(k) = k^2 - k^2 + 4k - 12 = 4k - 12$.

walkthrough.text:
Factor $-1$ out of the quadratic and linear terms in $x$:
$$h(x) = -(x^2 - 2kx) - (k^2 - 4k + 12)$$

Complete the square for $x^2 - 2kx$:
$$x^2 - 2kx = (x - k)^2 - k^2$$
$$h(x) = -\left((x - k)^2 - k^2\right) - (k^2 - 4k + 12)$$

Distribute the negative sign and combine the terms in $k$:
$$= -(x - k)^2 + k^2 - k^2 + 4k - 12 = (4k - 12) - (x - k)^2$$
Thus $M(k) = 4k - 12$.

ai_rubric.observable: Factors $-1$ to write $-(x^2 - 2kx) - (k^2 - 4k + 12)$ and forms $(x - k)^2$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solves maximum condition for literal parameter k and evaluates vertex.

hints: The maximum value of $(4k - 12) - (x - k)^2$ is $M(k) = 4k - 12$.
Solve for $k$: $4k = 8 \implies k = 2$.
The vertex occurs at $x = k = 2$ with maximum value $y = -4$, so vertex is $(2, -4)$.

walkthrough.text:
The maximum value of $h(x)$ is $M(k)$ because $-(x - k)^2 \le 0$:
$$\text{Maximum value} = 4k - 12$$

Set the maximum value equal to $-4$ and solve for $k$:
$$4k - 12 = -4 \implies 4k = 8 \implies k = 2$$

State the coordinates of the vertex $(x_v, y_v) = (k, -4)$:
$$\text{Vertex} = (2, -4)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains $k = 2$ and states the vertex coordinates as $(2, -4)$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: comparison of two parabolas in special completed square forms (one positive non-monic (2x+a)^2+b, one negative monic c - (x-d)^2), finding minimum and maximum turning points and computing the exact segment length.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Requires completing the square into (2x + a)^2 + b to find minimum point P.

hints: Expand $(2x + a)^2 + b = 4x^2 + 4ax + a^2 + b$.
Equate linear coefficients: $4a = -4 \implies a = -1$.
Compute $a^2 + b = 6 \implies 1 + b = 6 \implies b = 5$, giving $y = (2x - 1)^2 + 5$.
Find the minimum point $P$ where $2x - 1 = 0 \implies x = \frac{1}{2}, y = 5$, giving $P\left(\frac{1}{2}, 5\right)$.

walkthrough.text:
Complete the square for $C_1$ in the form $(2x + a)^2 + b$:
$$(2x + a)^2 + b = 4x^2 + 4ax + a^2 + b$$
$$4a = -4 \implies a = -1$$
$$(-1)^2 + b = 6 \implies 1 + b = 6 \implies b = 5$$
$$y = (2x - 1)^2 + 5$$

Determine the minimum point $P$ where $2x - 1 = 0$:
$$2x = 1 \implies x = \frac{1}{2}, \quad y = 5$$
$$P = \left(\frac{1}{2}, 5\right) \quad (\text{or } (0.5, 5))$$

ai_rubric.observable: Expands $(2x + a)^2 + b = 4x^2 + 4ax + a^2 + b$ and equates coefficients to find $a = -1$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Requires negative completing the square for C_2, finding maximum point Q, and calculating distance PQ.

hints: The maximum point $Q$ occurs at $x = 3, y = 20$, giving $Q(3, 20)$.
Use the distance formula between $P\left(\frac{1}{2}, 5\right)$ and $Q(3, 20)$: $\sqrt{\left(3 - \frac{1}{2}\right)^2 + (20 - 5)^2}$.
Evaluate $\sqrt{\left(\frac{5}{2}\right)^2 + 15^2} = \sqrt{\frac{25}{4} + \frac{900}{4}} = \sqrt{\frac{925}{4}} = \frac{5\sqrt{37}}{2}$.

walkthrough.text:
Complete the square for $C_2: y = 11 + 6x - x^2$:
$$y = -(x^2 - 6x) + 11 = -\left((x - 3)^2 - 9\right) + 11 = 20 - (x - 3)^2$$
So $c = 20$ and $d = 3$.

Identify the maximum point $Q$:
$$x_Q = 3, \quad y_Q = 20 \implies Q = (3, 20)$$

Apply the Euclidean distance formula between $P\left(\frac{1}{2}, 5\right)$ and $Q(3, 20)$:
$$PQ = \sqrt{\left(3 - \frac{1}{2}\right)^2 + (20 - 5)^2} = \sqrt{\left(\frac{5}{2}\right)^2 + 15^2}$$
$$PQ = \sqrt{\frac{25}{4} + 225} = \sqrt{\frac{25 + 900}{4}} = \sqrt{\frac{925}{4}} = \frac{5\sqrt{37}}{2} \quad (\text{or } \approx 15.2)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Completes the square on $C_2$ to obtain $y = 20 - (x - 3)^2$ and identifies maximum point $Q(3, 20)$.
